options: Lying flat (orthopnea) or waking gasping at night
Known liver disease or previous hepatitis

history.ask: Smoking, chronic cough, or known chest disease
Cold intolerance, weight gain, dry skin

options: Varicose veins or previous leg vein clot
One leg first, then the other

red_flags: Swelling with breathlessness at rest or orthopnea — decompensating heart failure
Strictly unilateral painful swollen leg — deep vein thrombosis
Rapid facial plus leg swelling with frothy urine — acute nephrotic/nephritic process
exam: Confirm pitting vs non-pitting and mark the upper level (ankle, knee, thigh, sacrum)
Auscultate the heart: gallop rhythm, murmurs, loud P2
Auscultate the lung bases: crackles, stony dullness of effusion
Examine the abdomen: shifting dullness, hepatomegaly (tender or pulsatile), splenomegaly
Search for chronic liver stigmata: spider nevi, palmar erythema, gynecomastia
Check thyroid signs: dry coarse skin, delayed ankle-reflex relaxation
Inspect leg skin: hemosiderin staining, venous eczema, ulcers, varicosities
Compare calves: warmth, tenderness, circumference difference

investigations.why: Heavy proteinuria rules nephrotic syndrome in with one dipstick; mild proteinuria with hematuria points instead to CKD — the single highest-yield test in edema
Raised creatinine rules chronic kidney disease in and grades it; also baseline before any diuresis decision by the treating doctor
Low albumin unifies nephrotic syndrome and cirrhosis; deranged liver enzymes and low albumin together support cirrhosis
Normocytic anemia supports CKD; macrocytosis supports chronic liver disease
Raised TSH rules hypothyroid (non-pitting) myxedema in when cold intolerance and delayed reflexes are present
Old infarction or left ventricular strain supports heart failure; P pulmonale with right-axis deviation supports cor pulmonale
Cardiomegaly with congestion or effusion rules cardiac edema in; hyperinflation supports cor pulmonale from chronic lung disease
Confirms heart failure (ejection fraction) and estimates pulmonary pressure for cor pulmonale — the arbiter when ECG/CXR are equivocal
Coarse shrunken liver with ascites rules cirrhosis in; small echogenic kidneys rule chronic kidney disease in
If swelling is asymmetric, painful, or one leg started first: rules deep vein thrombosis in or out

supports: Exertional dyspnea, orthopnea, or nocturnal gasping
Marked pitting edema in an otherwise well-looking patient
Known liver disease, hepatitis, or alcohol history
Ascites preceding or exceeding the leg swelling
Hemosiderin staining, venous eczema, or ulcers
Swelling worse by evening, better in the morning
Swelling began after starting amlodipine/nifedipine, NSAIDs, or steroids
Cold intolerance, weight gain, dry skin
Chronic cough, smoking, or known chest disease
Non-pitting woody swelling of months to years
No cardiac, renal, or hepatic findings
Strictly one leg, painful, or one leg first
Calf tenderness, warmth, and circumference difference
